pr_title: Feature(harness): `canned_messages` project sets and build folding
verdict: NOT READY TO MERGE - important: I1, I2, I3, I4, I5
strengths: The canned_messages key lands in all four required places (defaults.json, harness.schema.json, CannedSet plus `_canned_messages` in config.py, README key row), and the loader re-checks the shape without jsonschema.

Receipt, ActionPlan, SkillSpec and DesignEvolutionCatalog schemas are generated from their pydantic models and guarded by byte-level drift tests, so the committed JSON cannot silently diverge from the models.

The breaking DesignEvolutionCatalog rewrite (closed levels, category_enums and summary tallies removed, id_conventions restructured) ships with a concrete migration paragraph in plugins/harness/schemas/README.md.

Schema descriptions state honestly what the JSON schema cannot enforce (Provenance commit/staged rule, SkillSpec plugin_dir/target exclusivity, DesignEvolution cross-record rules), pointing writers at the model APIs.
The ActionPlan `frozen` description matches `plan_doc.frozen_digest` exactly for both the receipts scheme (every field but `frozen`) and the sealed/unset schemes.
Every new suite is behavioral: drivers run in-process through `main` against make_project git repos, and no test stubs the function under test.

The test_config_canned_messages.py cases run each malformed set both with jsonschema and with it hidden (`sys.modules['jsonschema'] = None`), which reaches the builder's own check because config.py imports jsonschema lazily.
Receipt seal tests change one sealed field at a time and also cover the item's planned files, planned tests, plan id and item id, so each part of the seal input is pinned.
test_strap_rounds.py pins backward compatibility by recomputing the pre-rounds driver digest and checking that an empty `rounds` leaves it unchanged.
The sealed_first_freeze fixture patches plan_record.FIRST_SCHEME, which is read at call time. That keeps the older sealed and legacy suites on their scheme without forking them.
fold_canned unit tests cover appear, join, vanish, pending and input immutability, and integration tests add the negative case (a non-canned file still fails with `is in no commit`).
config._canned_set checks the canned_messages shape without jsonschema, with a json-path-style location per bad entry, so a load on the floor install still refuses a malformed set.
fold_canned copies its input, leaves globbed entries and every non-canned path to the existing coverage check, and keeps the pending one-commit shape by joining the first block.
The RecordBook protocol (SealedBook / ReceiptBook) lets check, freeze, red, lanes, record and verify read item states one way under either scheme instead of branching in each command.
pin_scheme checks receipts before sealed with the same three proofs (stored, digest, HEAD copy), so a hand-deleted scheme cannot downgrade a receipts plan on refreeze.
Receipt seals bind plan id, item id and the item's frozen files and tests, so a copied receipt or a refreeze that moves the item's files breaks the seal visibly.
The HTML PIP builds all live content with textContent and escapes the embedded config's '<', so receipt or catalog text cannot inject markup.

branch-commit-msg SKILL.md:167-170 describes build folding exactly as canned_fold.fold_canned implements it (join the block carrying the set's message, the one block of a pending skeleton, else a new block at the end; vanished paths drop with emptied blocks; any other late file still fails coverage).

The README canned_messages key row states the matching rule (a `/` pattern matches the whole path, any other the file name) and precedence (project sets first) in the same terms as canned_messages._matches and get_canned_message.

write-plan SKILL.md step 9 heredoc names real symbols throughout (evolution_api.next_id/add, ChangePhase.post_exec_start, IssueCategory.signature_mismatch, OutcomeCategory.execution_blocker and the five change models), so it runs as written.
The new write-plan README separates developer-facing lifecycle from the agent procedure and matches plan.py's render contract (render writes a frozen receipts plan's page only when missing).

strap-skills SKILL.md's reopen paragraph matches strap.py's _reopen_base_problems (ancestor of HEAD, descends from the previous base, parts identical to the working tree) and its printed `reopen [done]` line, and spells out the strip-and-restore base that rule forces.
Plan 1012 records its four decisions with rationales and four sealed receipts with no deviations, and v0.7.1.md is retitled so the superseded release cannot be cut by mistake.

merge_commit_msg.py:275 swaps in project_canned_message inside render, which runs only after main has called activate(load_config(...)) at line 475, so the new active() read never happens before activation.

strap-skills reopen prose (SKILL.md:242-263) matches strap.py exactly: the printed `reopen [done] | <name> | round <N> | base <sha12> | was <hash12>` line (strap.py:937), the ancestor and descendant base rules and the parts-equal-to-base rule (_reopen_base_problems), red skipping earlier-round greens (_red_plan), and the tests/kind lock (strap_api._refuse_fields).

The write-plan step 9 heredoc names only symbols that exist: evolution_api.next_id/add, the ChangePhase/IssueCategory/OutcomeCategory members and the ChangeOriginal/ChangeIssue/NewOutcome/WhyNewOutcome fields. Its refusal claims (duplicate id, unknown item) match _duplicate_ids and evolution_doc.plan_problems.

The deviation-flag contract in write-plan SKILL.md:166-175 and README.md:75-87 (--also, --substitute, --cite binding the uncited deviations before it, --sha/--staged required) agrees with plan.py's record docstring and DEVIATION_FLAGS handling.

branch-commit-msg's build-folding paragraph (SKILL.md:167-170) matches canned_fold.fold_canned: pending joins the first block, otherwise the block whose message equals the canned message, otherwise a new block at the end, and a vanished entry drops along with any block it empties.
Every relative link in the new write-plan README (../../scripts/plan.py, ../../lib/harness_lib/*_models.py, ../parallel2/README.md) resolves at the head.

The canned_messages key touches all four required places (defaults.json, harness.schema.json, the CannedSet dataclass and _canned_messages builder in config.py, the README key table), and the builder check runs without jsonschema too, with parametrized tests for both paths.
Plan 1012 matches the code: D1-D4 (list shape, project sets first, fold, drop) are each implemented as decided, and `plan.py check` passes on plans 1012, 1013 and 1014 at the head.
fold_canned is a pure function on a copied CommitDict, tested alone and through run_build, including the case where a non-canned file that appeared still fails coverage.
run_build captures once and passes the same capture to the fold and to coverage_problems, which removes the second capture_branch call.

The receipts scheme keeps old plans valid: FIRST_SCHEME is read at call time, the existing sealed and legacy suites patch it to sealed, and pin_scheme checks receipts before sealed with the stored, digest and HEAD-copy rules.
The HTML PIP loader builds the DOM only with textContent and escapes `<` in the inline config, so plan and receipt text cannot inject markup.
SkillSpec.rounds stays out of the dump and the driver digest when empty, and test_strap_rounds pins the old digest byte for byte.
New tests are behavioural: driver suites run plan.py and strap.py against make_project repos, and the only monkeypatches change a config constant or stdin, never the function under test.

The canned_messages key touches all four required places together: defaults.json, harness.schema.json, the config.py CannedSet dataclass and builder, and the README row. The builder repeats the schema's shape check, so a load without jsonschema refuses the same malformed sets, and test_config_canned_messages.py runs every malformed case both with and without jsonschema.

The DesignEvolution migration steps are word-for-word the same in schemas/README.md Migration and the v1.0.0 Breaking changes, and they match the closed models: drop $schema, _comment and category_enums, move id_conventions prefixes, and drop the tallies that counts() now computes.

The receipts lifecycle reads the same way in the plan.py docstring, write-plan SKILL.md, the write-plan README and the schemas README: render on a frozen receipts page, the digest scope per scheme, refreeze tolerance with the 're-record after refreeze' line, and the deviation flags needing --sha or --staged on a receipts plan.

The strap reopen docs match the code. SKILL.md step 12, the strap.py docstring and the README row agree with cmd_reopen and _reopen_base_problems (ancestor of HEAD, descendant of the previous base, every part clean at the base), with _red_plan skipping GREEN behaviors, and with strap_api locking tests and kind after an earlier round.

Receipt.schema.json and the regenerated DesignEvolutionCatalog.schema.json both come from models through gen_plan_schema.py, and a contract test checks them for drift, so the schemas README 'generated, never edited' claims hold.

The new tests are behavioral, with no mock-chain wiring. canned_fold is tested as a pure function and again through run_build on a real cloned repository, and project canned sets are tested through capture and merge render under an activated make_project config.

important.name: write-plan SkillSpec pins branch-only commits; a squash merge orphans them
important.summary: docs/plans/strap/write-plan/SkillSpec.json stores `base` 9368d9e (line 4) and round bases 84cc5bc (line 889) and b7c6209 (line 908). 9368d9e and b7c6209 exist only on 1150-canned-messages (b7c6209 is contained by no branch but this one and its backups). strap.py relies on these SHAs after the merge: `reopen` refuses unless `merge-base --is-ancestor <spec.base> <new base>` holds (strap.py:908-913), and an edit-mode baseline reads SKILL.md at `base`. A squash or rebase merge of this PR leaves both commits unreachable from main, so the next `strap.py reopen write-plan` fails with `does not descend from the previous base`, and baseline runs fail once the commits are pruned or on any clone without the branch. Plans 1012/1013/1014 also pin `frozen.commit` b4e8d6b, but nothing compares that SHA with HEAD, so only the strap spec breaks.
fix: Merge PR 266 with a merge commit (no squash, no rebase), so 9368d9e and b7c6209 stay reachable from main.
If a squash merge is required: after the merge, reopen write-plan on a main commit and refreeze it, so `base` and the round bases name commits main keeps.

important.name: write-plan strap fixtures carry the developer's absolute checkout path
important.summary: The frozen plan fixtures laid into scenario trees hold commands such as `sh "E:/automation/operator-straps/plugins/harness/scripts/hpy" "E:/automation/operator-straps/plugins/harness/scripts/strap.py" reopen write-plan ...` (plan-1014 JSON lines 196, 232, 236; its PIP lines 122, 134-135; plan-1021 JSON line 198 and PIP line 122). The live plan `docs/plans/1014_strap_reopen_ActionPlan.json` was since rewritten to repo-relative `sh plugins/harness/scripts/hpy plugins/harness/scripts/strap.py ...` (lines 196, 232, 236), so the fixtures are the only tracked copies left with a machine path. They publish a local path in a public marketplace repo, and they point a scenario agent that follows the plan text at the developer's real checkout instead of `TREE`, the very leak the new strap-scenario-runner snapshot/`problem:` rule (strap-scenario-runner.md:42-55) and the 'a path ... outside TREE stands for the same repo-relative path under TREE' sentence were added to paper over.
fix: Re-lay the plan-1014 fixture from the current frozen plan 1014 (repo-relative commands) and its page, and rewrite the plan-1021 fixture command to the repo-relative form, refreezing each fixture plan so its digest holds; rerun the affected write-plan scenarios if the SkillSpec pins the fixture content.

If the fixtures must stay byte-identical to what the frozen write-plan round ran against, record that decision in the write-plan SkillSpec or plan 1014 DesignEvolution and replace the drive letter path with a placeholder in a later round.

important.name: Project canned messages are never checked against the commit-message rules
important.summary:
The `canned_messages` contract accepts any non-empty `message` (schema `minLength: 1`, harness.schema.json:118; `_canned_set` in config.py:374-383 checks only the shape). The built-in sets are pinned by `test_every_canned_message_passes_the_message_checks` (tests/lib/test_canned_messages.py:90-94) because `branch_commit_msg.py build` runs `commit_txt.message_problems` on every block: the strict subject rule `^(?:Feature|Fix|Refactor|Test|Build|Docs|Chore)(?:\(...\))?: \S` (commit_txt.py:47), vendor names, filler, double quotes. A project set such as `{"patterns": ["docs/TODO/*"], "message": "Update TODO files"}` loads cleanly, is prefilled at capture as `message: canned`, and the c-msg / branch-commit-msg skills tell the agent to keep a canned message as it stands, so every build of a matching block fails on a message the agent was told not to change. Nothing in the schema description warns that the message must pass those checks, and no test covers a non-conforming project set.

Also (config): The description at harness.schema.json:111 says a pattern holding a `/` matches the whole repo-relative path with fnmatch, case-sensitive (`fnmatchcase`, canned_messages.py:50-53). fnmatch `*` also matches `/`, so `docs/TODO/*.json` matches `docs/TODO/archive/old.json` too, widening the set beyond what a glob reader expects. The sibling key `review.tracking_paths` (harness.schema.json:91) documents exactly this caveat; this one does not, nor does the README row (README.md:497).

Also (config): harness.schema.json:111 ends "Read by branch-commit-msg, c-msg and merge-commit-msg." amend-commit-msg runs the same `branch_commit_msg.py` capture (which calls `project_canned_message`, branch_commit_msg.py:306,354) and its SKILL.md:63-64 now documents project sets under `canned_messages`. The README row (README.md:497) has the same three-skill list.
fix: Validate each project message at config load: in `_canned_set` (config.py:374-383), or in a check `project_canned_message` runs once, build the entry with `commit_txt.entry_from_message` and raise `ConfigError(f"{where}/message: ...")` with the `message_problems` lines; add a test in tests/lib/test_config_canned_messages.py that a set with a non-conforming subject is refused.

If an import from config.py into commit_txt is unwanted, have `project_canned_message` skip (and report via a `problem:` line at capture) a project set whose message fails `message_problems`, and state in the harness.schema.json `canned_messages` description and the README key row that `message` must pass the commit subject rule (`Word(scope): summary` with Feature/Fix/Refactor/Test/Build/Docs/Chore), no double quotes and no vendor names.
Append to the `canned_messages` description at harness.schema.json:111 and the README row at README.md:497: "fnmatch `*` crosses `/`, so `docs/*.md` also matches nested files."
Change the sentence at harness.schema.json:111 to "Read by branch-commit-msg, amend-commit-msg, c-msg and merge-commit-msg." and add `amend-commit-msg` to the README.md:497 row.

important.name: Build folding is never run with a project canned set
important.summary:
The module docstring (lines 3-5) says a project set's regenerated file must not fail build. Every TestBuildFolds case uses the built-in TODO set, and the clone fixture has no `canned_messages` config. The unit cases pass `_canned` (lines 29-30), which calls get_canned_message without `extra`. If branch_commit_msg.py:554 passed get_canned_message instead of project_canned_message, every test here would still pass, and a project report written after capture would fail build with `is in no commit`. That project-set-plus-build-folding path is the headline feature of this PR.

Also (tests): fold_canned treats a captured path that an existing glob entry stands for as claimed (canned_fold.py:28, through expand_entry). `_drop_vanished` keeps a block whose file list was already empty (canned_fold.py:41, `kept or not files`). Neither case has a test, so a change that re-places glob-covered canned paths, or drops empty blocks, would go unnoticed.
fix: Add a TestBuildFolds case on a clone whose upstream make_project config sets `canned_messages` (for example `{"patterns": ["offlineTestReport.json"], "message": "Chore(tests): refresh the offline test report"}`). Write `offlineTestReport.json` after `run_capture`, run `run_build`, and assert a new block with that file and the project message.
Or point `_canned` at project_canned_message under an activated config that holds a project set, and add a unit case where a project-set path appears.

Add a TestFoldCanned case with a block holding a glob entry (for example `docs/TODO/*.json` with CANNED_TODO), where TODO appears in `captured`, and assert the result is unchanged. Add a case with a `([], "Feature: x")` block and assert it survives.

important.name: Second-reopen test cannot tell the last round's hash from the first
important.summary: test_second_reopen_appends_a_round never changes a part file between round 1 and round 2, and strap.py skill_hash (plugins/harness/scripts/strap.py:219-221) hashes only the part files. So `second` equals `frozen`, and the assertions at 262, 264 and 266 hold either way. A freeze that names rounds[0] instead of the last round, or a reopen that copies the wrong round's stamp, would still pass. The module docstring (line 5) says the next freeze names the last round's hash, and nothing here pins that.
fix: After the first `reopen` and before its `freeze`, rewrite SKILL (for example body `Round two.`). Then add `assert second != frozen` after line 255 so lines 262-266 can tell the rounds apart. The `commit_all` at 257 already commits the edit before the second reopen.

minor.name: README Canned messages section still describes only the built-in table
minor.summary: The README section that explains canned messages (README.md:296-322) says the entries live in `lib/harness_lib/canned_messages.py`, lists only the two built-in sets, and ends with 'a project that renames them drafts as usual'. It never mentions the new `canned_messages` key (project sets tried first, `canned_messages.py:61-70`) or that `branch_commit_msg.py build` now folds a canned file that appeared or vanished after capture (`canned_fold.py:18-32`). The key-table row (README.md:497) also names only `c-msg`, `branch-commit-msg` and `merge-commit-msg`, while `amend-commit-msg` captures through the same `project_canned_message` path and its SKILL.md:63-64 says project sets apply.
fix: Add a bullet to the Canned messages section: a project adds its own sets under `canned_messages` in `.claude/harness.json`, tried in order before the built-in entries, and `build` folds a canned file that appeared or vanished since capture; change line 321-322 to say a project that renames the files can name them in a project set.
Add `amend-commit-msg` to the consumer list of the `canned_messages` key-table row.

minor.name: v1.0.0 release body: canned line lacks its PR number and the file carries working notes
minor.summary: Every change line in docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md names its PR (#253, #255, #257, #261, #262) except the canned-messages line (line 63), which lands through #266; #261 and #262 were merged into this branch, so #266 is also the PR that brings them to main. The 'Notes for the release' section (lines 69-73) is branch bookkeeping (plan 1012's bump, the superseded v0.7.1 file); the project rule makes this file the GitHub release body verbatim, so those notes would ship in the published release.
fix: Prefix line 63 with `#266` and drop the 'Notes for the release' section (or move its content to the PR description) before the release is cut.

minor.name: fold_canned matches a canned block by exact message while the receipt tag strips
minor.summary: _place joins an appeared canned path to a block only when folded[k][1] == canned([...files, path]) exactly, while branch_commit_msg._receipt_line tags a block [canned] on commit.message.strip() == canned.strip(). A canned block whose skeleton message carries a stray trailing newline or space is therefore recognised as canned in the receipt but not by the fold, which then appends a second block with the same canned header instead of joining the existing one.
fix: Compare stripped messages in _place: `(folded[k][1] or '').strip() == (canned([*folded[k][0], path]) or '').strip()`, matching _receipt_line.

minor.name: canned_messages key docs omit that project sets also drive build-time folding
minor.summary: The canned_messages module docstring, the schema description and the README key row describe a project set only as a message source. Since run_build passes project_canned_message to fold_canned, every file a project set covers is also silently added to or dropped from the skeleton's blocks at build when it appeared or vanished after capture, bypassing the coverage check for those files. A project that writes a broad pattern (for example *.md) gets that behaviour without the key's documentation mentioning it; only the branch-commit-msg skill does.
fix: Add one sentence to the canned_messages docstring, the schema description and the README row: files a set covers that appear or vanish between capture and build are folded into the blocks (harness_lib.canned_fold), so a set should cover generated files only.

minor.name: has_canned_message ignores the project's canned sets
minor.summary: canned_messages.has_canned_message (canned_messages.py:78-80) calls get_canned_message without `extra`, so it answers False for a change that a project `canned_messages` set covers. Every driver call site moved to project_canned_message, so this public helper is now the only lookup that disagrees with the drivers. It is used only by tests today, but a future caller would get the built-in answer without warning.
fix: Give has_canned_message an `extra: Sequence[CannedSet] = ()` parameter passed through to get_canned_message, and state in its docstring that it checks the built-in LOOKUP unless `extra` is given.
Or add project_has_canned_message beside project_canned_message.

minor.name: evolution_api writes live.js for an unfrozen plan, contradicting the plan.py and plan_render_html docstrings
minor.summary:
evolution_api._save (evolution_api.py:79-86) always calls plan_live.write_live, and also writes the plan folder's .gitignore. HARNESS_RULES and write-plan SKILL step 8 now send spec-review changes to `evolution_api.add` right after `plan.py new`, before the freeze, so an unfrozen plan gets a live.js. plan.py:28 says "A plan not frozen yet has no ``live.js``", plan_render_html.py:10-11 says "Only a plan frozen with receipts has a sidecar", and test_write_pip_writes_no_sidecar_for_a_plan_not_yet_frozen pins that for write_pip. The unfrozen page has no loader, so the file does nothing, but the docstrings are wrong.

Also (system_shape): plan_render_html.py:10-11 states that only a plan frozen with receipts has a live.js sidecar, and that an unfrozen plan's page carries no loader. evolution_api._save (evolution_api.py:79-86) calls plan_live.write_live on every save, whatever the plan's scheme. Two documented paths reach it with no receipts freeze: write-plan SKILL.md step 8 and HARNESS_RULES.md enter a spec-review change once `plan.py new` has run (the plan is unfrozen), and they enter a post-freeze design change on a sealed plan 'under either scheme'. Both paths leave a `<plans>/<id>/live.js` plus a driver-written `.gitignore` in the plan folder. On a sealed plan nothing reads that file, because the sealed plan has a markdown PIP and no HTML page. tests/lib/test_evolution_api.py:87-90 pins the write on an unfrozen plan, so code and test agree with each other but not with the renderer's contract.
fix: In evolution_api._save, call plan_live.write_live only when plan_receipts.uses_receipts(plan) is true, and say so in the module docstring ("Each save rebuilds the live.js of a frozen receipts plan").
Or reword plan.py:28 and plan_render_html.py:10-11 to say an evolution_api save also writes live.js on an unfrozen plan.

Guard the sidecar write in evolution_api._save with `if plan_receipts.uses_receipts(plan): plan_live.write_live(...)`. Change the module docstring (lines 9-10) to 'on a receipts plan each save rebuilds live.js', and change test_add_rebuilds_live_js to freeze the plan under receipts first, adding a test that a sealed or unfrozen plan gets no live.js. freeze already writes live.js through write_pip, so an unfrozen plan's catalog still reaches the page at freeze.
Keep the behavior and correct the contract instead: change plan_render_html.py:10-11 to say that evolution_api also writes live.js on any plan, and that only a frozen receipts page loads it.

minor.name: pip_document pattern now admits absolute and machine paths
minor.summary: The widened `pip_document` pattern `^.+_PIP\.(md|html)$` (ActionPlan.schema.json:671, generated from plan_models.py:174) dropped the `docs/PLANS/` prefix, which correctly removes a project literal (plans live under the configurable `artifacts.plans`), but it also dropped the only thing that kept the value repo-relative. `C:/Users/x/proj/docs/plans/0001_T_PIP.html` or a backslash path now validates and can land in a tracked plan JSON. The harness config schema already pins relative paths with `relPath` (`^(?![/\x5c])(?![A-Za-z]:)`, harness.schema.json:9); the plan model has no equivalent. Plan 1013 itself specified `^docs/PLANS/.+_PIP\.(md|html)$` (docs/plans/1013_plan_receipts_ActionPlan.json:169), so the relative anchor was intended.
fix: In plan_models.py:174 change the pattern to `r"^(?![/\\])(?![A-Za-z]:)[^\\]+_PIP\.(md|html)$"` (relative, forward slashes only), regenerate ActionPlan.schema.json with tools/gen_plan_schema.py, and add a case to `test_a_pip_document_may_be_html` that an absolute path is refused.

minor.name: Status rules say every item terminates COMPLETE, next to a rule that keeps receipts items PENDING
minor.summary: schemas/README.md:61 now says that on a receipts plan 'the item stays `PENDING` in the JSON' and the receipt is the proof, but line 63 still reads unqualified 'every item must terminate in COMPLETE or CLOSED_NO_ACTION'. On a receipts plan the JSON status never terminates; only the receipt outcome does. Line 280 likewise still points `markdown_section` at a Markdown section, while receipts plans render an HTML page.
fix: Qualify line 63: 'every item must terminate in COMPLETE or CLOSED_NO_ACTION (in its receipt on a receipts plan, in the JSON on a plan frozen before receipts)', and scope line 280 to plans with a markdown PIP.

minor.name: schemas README calls the plan key of primary_documents a rule the schema cannot express
minor.summary: In the new DesignEvolutionCatalog section, schemas/README.md:202 lists 'the `plan` key in `primary_documents`' first among the cross-record rules that 'the generated schema' cannot express. The generated catalogs/DesignEvolutionCatalog.schema.json:339-345 does express it: `primary_documents` carries `"required": ["plan"]` from evolution_models.py:141-143 (`json_schema_extra={"required": ["plan"]}`). A reader who trusts line 202 would wrongly expect a schema-only validator to accept a catalog without `plan`. The other three listed rules really are validator-only.
fix: Delete 'the `plan` key in `primary_documents`, ' from schemas/README.md:202, so the list starts with 'unique change ids'.

minor.name: Workflow Step 2 says render after freeze writes the PIP; on a receipts plan it rebuilds only live.js
minor.summary: The Step 2 flow in schemas/README.md:223-224 runs `plan.py render <id>` after `freeze` and annotates it '(writes the PIP from the JSON: HTML with live.js on a receipts plan, ...)'. The code does something narrower. plan_render_html.refresh_pip (lines 210-221) and the plan.py docstring (lines 25-29) both say that on a frozen receipts plan render rebuilds live.js and writes the page only when it is missing. The write-plan README (lines 20-22, 45) and the same file's Step 3 (line 239) say the same, so line 224 is the one place that contradicts them.
fix: Reword the annotation at schemas/README.md:224 to '(a frozen receipts plan: rebuilds live.js, and the HTML page only when missing; a plan frozen before receipts: rewrites the markdown PIP)'.

minor.name: _folded_document re-implements document_from_payload, leaving the latter test-only
minor.summary:
run_build now builds its document through _folded_document, which repeats document_from_payload's parsing of commits, merge_base and pending. document_from_payload has no caller left under plugins/ (only tests/scripts/test_branch_commit_msg.py), so the two parsers can drift: a change to how the payload's merge_base or pending is read in one is not seen by the other, and the tests exercise the copy the build no longer uses.

Also (overall): run_build now adds a canned-set file that appeared after capture to a block, or removes one that vanished (branch_commit_msg.py:547-556, canned_fold.fold_canned). The receipt that the skill tells the agent to relay unchanged lists headers only (_receipt_line, branch_commit_msg.py:612). A developer who reads only that receipt is not told that the TXT now stages a file nobody reviewed at capture time, such as a regenerated TODO catalog. The SKILL.md paragraph documents the behaviour, but each run gives no sign of it.

Also (overall): run_build now builds its document through _folded_document (branch_commit_msg.py:547-556). That function repeats document_from_payload's merge_base normalization and pending flag, and adds the fold. document_from_payload (branch_commit_msg.py:509-514) is now called only by tests/scripts/test_branch_commit_msg.py:1168, so the two payload-to-document paths can drift apart.
fix: Give document_from_payload an optional `captures` argument that applies fold_canned, and have run_build call it instead of _folded_document.
Or have document_from_payload delegate to _folded_document(payload, notes, None) so one parser remains.
Have fold_canned return the paths it placed and dropped, and add one receipt line per change (e.g. `folded: + docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json -> 3`, `folded: - <path>`) before the final line.
Give document_from_payload an optional `captures` argument that runs fold_canned, have run_build call it, and delete _folded_document.
Or have _folded_document call document_from_payload with the folded commits substituted into a copied payload.

minor.name: Markdown-PIP detection differs between write_pip and the first freeze
minor.summary: _keeps_markdown treats documentation as the markdown PIP when only its file name matches pip_path(plan_file).name, but move_documentation moves it only when the whole value equals rel(repo, pip_path(plan_file)). A plan whose documentation names the PIP by another spelling of the same file (folder case on Windows, a backslash path, a ./ prefix) keeps the markdown PIP before freeze, yet at the first receipts freeze documentation is not moved and the markdown PIP is not deleted: the HTML page is written beside a stale markdown PIP that documentation still points to, and P3 stays silent because that file exists.
fix: Use one predicate in both places, for example a helper in plan_render_html that compares Path(doc).name to pip_path(plan_file).name, and call it from move_documentation.

minor.name: write-plan README lifecycle diagram routes a design change to evolution_api instead of a refreeze
minor.summary: The diagram at README.md:31-33 labels the loop 'design changed? evolution_api.add, cite it on the record'. SKILL.md:97-99 and 137-175, and README.md:67-70, separate two paths. A design change the developer asks for is a `write` plus `freeze --refreeze`, plus a catalog entry. Work found during execution to depart from its item (a deviation) goes to evolution_api.add and is cited with --also/--substitute/--cite. The diagram shows only the second path under the first one's name, so a reader could skip the refreeze for a real design change.
fix: Relabel the loop at README.md:33 as 'deviation found? evolution_api.add, cite it on the record', and add a second arrow or a note: 'design change asked for? plan_api.write + freeze --refreeze (developer OK)'.

minor.name: write-plan README Render row disagrees with its own PIP paragraph
minor.summary: README.md:45 says `PLAN render <id>` writes '`live.js` (and the page if it is missing)'. README.md:20-22, and refresh_pip in plan_render_html.py:210-221, say that only holds for a frozen receipts plan. On any other plan, render calls write_pip and rebuilds the PIP, which is HTML for an unfrozen plan bound for receipts and markdown for a legacy plan. write_pip writes no live.js in either case, because uses_receipts is false until the freeze. A developer who reads only the lifecycle table expects an unfrozen plan's render to leave the page alone and to produce a live.js. Neither happens.
fix: Change the Render row's Writes cell at README.md:45 to: 'the PIP; on a frozen receipts plan only `live.js` (and the page if it is missing)'.

minor.name: write-plan step 9 example shows only the EX/post-exec-start id prefix that step 8 defers to
minor.summary: SKILL.md:97-101 has a developer-requested design change after the freeze, and a spec-review change (phase `spec-review`), entered through evolution_api.add 'built as step 9 shows'. The step 9 example at SKILL.md:142-163 hardcodes `next_id("<id>", "EX")` and `phase=ChangePhase.post_exec_start`, and the prose names only the `EX` prefix. The prefix map S=spec-review, P=plan-review, PR=pr-bot-review, EX/CX=post-exec-start appears only in DesignChange.id's field description (evolution_models.py:67-69). No validator ties prefix to phase, so an agent that copies the example for a spec-review change produces an EX id with phase spec-review, and the catalog accepts it silently.
fix: In SKILL.md step 8 (line 97-101) or step 9 (line 142-143), name the prefix for each phase: '`S` with `ChangePhase.spec_review`, `P` with `plan_review`, `PR` with `pr_bot_review`, `EX` with `post_exec_start`', and tell the reader to pass the matching prefix to `next_id`.
Add a DesignChange validator that rejects an id prefix that does not match its phase, so the mismatch fails when the change is built.
